newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says sets UK rates to meet inflation target.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says sets UK rates to meet inflation target.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he continued to set interest rates to meet his target of 2.5 percent or less for underlying inflation.
Asked on BBC Radio 4 if he would have to raise interest rates again following his budget on Tuesday, he replied:

"When I meet Eddie (George), sometimes I put interest rates up, sometimes I put them down according to what my judgement tells me is good for the real economy and people earning their living out there."

Clarke said that at his monthly monetary meetings with Bank of England Governor Eddie George, they examined the way the economy was going and set interest rates in order to keep inflation down to 2.5 percent.
Britain was now a stable and successful economy, Clarke said.
"And this is a sensible, virtuous budget. It has some good news, it has some bad news. Overall, it reduces taxation, certainly for the ordinary hard-working men and women of this country."
